paragraph: PAUL'S “HELPERS IN CHRIST JESUS” (ROMANS 16:3) · CALLED IN ACTS 18: PAUL FINDS THEM AT CORINTH

blocks.text: PAUL'S “HELPERS IN CHRIST JESUS” (ROMANS 16:3) · CALLED IN ACTS 18: PAUL FINDS THEM AT CORINTH
Priscilla and Aquila. A tentmaking couple who sheltered Paul, taught Apollos and kept a church in their house.
ALSO CALLED
Prisca
FROM
Aquila was “a certain Jew … born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”.
TRADE
Tentmakers: Paul “was of the same craft”, so “he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers”.
FAMILY
Husband and wife: “Aquila … with his wife Priscilla”.
WRITINGS
None
BACKGROUND
Home, trade and family
FROM
TRADE
FAMILY
Husband and wife: “Aquila … with his wife Priscilla”. Acts 18:2

From the textScripture never names one without the other. In the KJV Priscilla is named first three times out of six (Acts 18:18; Romans 16:3; 2 Timothy 4:19); in the site's Tischendorf Greek text and the Revised Version, four times, because they also put her first at Acts 18:26. Acts 18:2 Acts 18:18 Acts 18:26 Romans 16:3 1 Corinthians 16:19 2 Timothy 4:19
THE CALLING
The calling
“And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.”
Acts 18:3 (KJV) →
WHERE THEY WENT
Acts and after
Pontus · Aquila's birthplace. Acts 18:2
Rome · Left under Claudius's order; greeted here later. Acts 18:2 Romans 16:3–5
Italy · “lately come from Italy”. Acts 18:2
Corinth · Worked with Paul as tentmakers. Acts 18:1–3
Cenchreae · Port of Corinth; the vow. Acts 18:18
Ephesus · Taught Apollos; a church in their house. Acts 18:19 Acts 18:26 +2 more
Asia · The Apostolic Constitutions (4th century or earlier) name Aquila a bishop of “the parishes of Asia” (tradition). 1 Corinthians 16:19
IN ACTS AND THE LETTERS
At Corinth Paul lived and worked with them. Acts 18:2–3
When Paul left Corinth they sailed with him; he “left them” at Ephesus. Acts 18:18–19
At Ephesus they heard Apollos in the synagogue, “took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly”. Acts 18:26
From Ephesus they sent greetings to Corinth “with the church that is in their house”. 1 Corinthians 16:8 1 Corinthians 16:19

In Romans Paul greets them: “my helpers in Christ Jesus: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles”, and the church in their house. Romans 16:3–5
In 2 Timothy Paul asks Timothy to “Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus”. 2 Timothy 4:19

From the textActs 18:18 says “having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow”; the KJV's “his” is a supplied word, and the verse does not say plainly whether Paul or Aquila made the vow. Acts 18:18
COMPANIONS
Who was with them
Each line joins them to someone Scripture places beside them.
Paul Lodged and worked with them; they risked their necks for his life. Acts 18:3 Romans 16:3–4
Apollos They took him aside and taught him “the way of God more perfectly”. Acts 18:26
Timothy Paul asks him to greet them. 2 Timothy 4:19
Onesiphorus His household is greeted beside them. 2 Timothy 4:19
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
The last we read of them: Paul asks Timothy to greet them (2 Timothy 4:19). Scripture does not record their deaths. 2 Timothy 4:19
TRADITION SAYS

The Apostolic Constitutions list “Of the parishes of Asia, Aquila and Nicetas” among bishops ordained in the apostles' lifetime.[7] Who says so: Constitutions of the Holy Apostles 7.46, a compilation its ANF editor places “not later than the fourth century”
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
She was the more energetic, or stronger, of the two
Conybeare and Howson (1891); Kapp, ISBE (1915)

Conybeare and Howson: the order “conveys the impression that she was the more energetic character of the two”; Kapp: “The best explanation seems to be that she was the stronger character.” Romans 16:3 2 Timothy 4:19 [17][27]
She was of higher rank, and it was the custom among their friends
Ramsay (1895)
Ramsay: “Probably Prisca was of higher rank than her husband, for her name is that of a good old Roman family”; the order was “a conversational custom”. Acts 18:18 Romans 16:3 [16]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
Acts 18 Romans 16 1 Corinthians 16 2 Timothy 4
PASSAGES · 6
Acts 18:1–3 Acts 18:18–19 Acts 18:24–28 Romans 16:3–5 1 Corinthians 16:19 2 Timothy 4:19
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say when or where Priscilla and Aquila came to believe.
Scripture does not say how they risked their necks for Paul (Romans 16:4).
Scripture does not say which of them made the vow at Cenchrea, or that either of them wrote anything.
Scripture does not record their later life or deaths.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textActs always says Priscilla; 2 Timothy 4:19 says Prisca. In Romans 16:3 and 1 Corinthians 16:19 the KJV and the Textus Receptus read Priscilla, where Tischendorf's text and the Revised Version read Prisca. Acts 18:2 Romans 16:3 1 Corinthians 16:19 2 Timothy 4:19
Outside the BibleThe Roman biographer Suetonius records of Claudius: “Since the Jews constantly made disturbances at the instigation of Chrestus, he expelled them from Rome.”[10]

Scholars' viewRamsay (1895) and Kapp (ISBE, 1915) take this to be the order of Acts 18:2, and “Chrestus” as a garbled reference to Christ or his followers. Ramsay adds, from Dio Cassius, that the order was hard to enforce. Acts 18:2 [16][27]

Scholars' viewHarnack proposed Priscilla, with Aquila, as the writer of Hebrews; Dods (1897, 1910 printing) reports the case and answers that the writer speaks as one man. Hebrews 11:32 Hebrews 13:19 Hebrews 13:22–23 [14]
